titleEn: A Little Mouth Needs Little Bites!

pages.text: "I'll eat the biggest one in a single bite!" Pongi opened wide. Dad, in his overalls, pulled a fish onto the boat tied to a post. "Summer lunch!" The fish flapped and flapped.
Pongi put a whole fish in her mouth. Without chewing, gulp! Then another, gulp! "I'll fit them all in this tummy!" Dad said, "Slowly." But Pongi was already on her third fish.
Then suddenly, hic! Hic! Her throat felt tight. Pongi's mouth went round. The hiccups wouldn't stop. She stretched her neck and bent her back, but hic! Hic again!

Dad stroked Pongi's back and offered a bowl of water. Pongi took it in both paws and sipped. The hiccups slowly faded. "That was too big a mouthful. Shall I show you how to take little bites?" Pongi nodded.
Beside her, her little brother held a shell and nibbled tiny bits of shellfish. Munch, munch. Dad pointed. "Look! A little mouth needs little bites!" Pongi watched that little mouth.
Dad pretended to tap with her paws. "Your teeth are tapping hammers. If you put it all in at once, the hammers can't work." "So that's why it felt tight!" Pongi tapped her own teeth with a paw.

Pongi put just a little bit of fish into her mouth. Chew, chew, chew! One, two, three! "Oh! It tastes sweeter!" Pongi smiled and thumped her tail on the boat floor. "A little mouth needs little bites!"
After eating, her throat felt comfortable. No hiccups either. Her little brother held the shell and said, "Yum!" Pongi smiled. Only fish bones were left on the boat floor.
Pongi sang, "One, a little bit! Two, chew lots of times! Three, finish chewing, then swallow!" Dad untied the rope and rowed. The boat glided along. Pongi hummed and chewed.

Dad tied the boat in front of the house and hugged Pongi tight. "No more hiccups now, Pongi!" Small pieces and plenty of chewing make the flavor stronger and keep food from getting stuck. Pongi called, "A little mouth needs little bites!"
